touches.text: Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).

"it owns the gates only because we had to have some place to put them, but it does not control anything." The gates refuse on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.")
VERBS: crossing, watch, clear. clear is the PROVED gate it houses on the ticket's behalf.

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)

rehearsal: the cheapest model reads a ticket cold and tries to build it on paper, saying where it got stopped or what is missing. → CodeMother PURPOSE: training data, so graph trees learn to judge "buildable as written" without an LLM call. WHY: a simulation costs tokens; it earns them only by teaching a tree. It was never meant to catch every shortcoming of every ticket, and where it teaches nothing it costs more than the builder simply building and recording where it got stuck. (Akien 2026-11-02, measured that day: 1,721 rehearsal records, $888 recorded cost, no reader but the BUILDME gate.) So until a learner reads the records, a rehearsal is not a BUILDME requirement. The records stand as the learner's first corpus. The read's shape holds: it is handed the plan steps, the frame (intention, why, falsifier), and what exists and what does not, measured before the read. "Cold" means no conversation, history, chart or process, not blind to the disk. (Akien 2026-10-29.)
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. A failure is not automatically "it broke, change it". After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed. Either way the system improves, constantly. WHY: questions about a part are answered by its intention and why against the new thing's intention and why, so a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or to its implementation plan, never a conversation about procedure (Akien, 2026-11-02). The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure. It is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome: the ticket changes, or the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Nothing passes a ticket over a red; testing a sieve is what the ticket that fixes it does. (Q#62, Akien 2026-11-02.)

x, new or changed code (code-seam): at BUILDME the named proof exists and its PROVES names the ticket, and it may be red, since a new proof is red before its build. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured.
